request.description: I, Pencil: a pencil supply chain that keeps running. Loggers cut cedar in Oregon, a mill saws it into slats, graphite is mined in Sri Lanka and mixed with clay into leads, a factory in Pennsylvania glues leads into slats, paints them and adds erasers and brass ferrules, packs them into boxes, and trucks deliver the boxes to shops across the country, which sell them to customers.

world.label: Pencil Supply Chain
world.summary: A continuing supply chain turns cedar, graphite, and other materials into boxed pencils sold in shops across the country.

actions.description: Cut cedar and add logs to the logging crew's stock.
Use logs from the logging crew to make slats at the mill.
Mine graphite and add it to the miners' stock.
Use graphite from the miners and clay held at the lead works to make leads.
Use slats from the mill, leads from the lead works, and factory stocks of paint, erasers, and ferrules to make pencils.
Pack pencils into boxes held at the factory.
Carry packed pencils from the factory to a shop.
Sell pencils from a shop to a customer for the shop's listed price.

mechanics.rationale: Cutting cedar adds logs to the logging crew's stock; the represented stock is the only available measure of logs.
limits: The world has no represented cedar reserve, so the action cannot check or deplete one.
tests: A positive quantity adds that many logs to the logging crew's stock. A zero or negative quantity is refused.
semantic_bindings: quantity: logs cut and added to the logging crew's stock

mechanics.rationale: The mill uses logs held by the logging crew to make slats. The represented locations do not put the crew and mill together, so this trade is treated as an order from afar rather than requiring co-location.

checks.label: the logging crew has enough logs

limits: This is an immediate abstract order and does not represent a journey or its duration.
tests: With enough logs, the action subtracts the quantity from the logging crew and adds the same quantity of slats to the mill. Insufficient logs refuse the action.
semantic_bindings: source: logging crew supplying logs
quantity: logs consumed and slats produced

mechanics.rationale: Mining adds graphite to the miners' stock; no separate mine reserve is represented.
limits: The world has no represented graphite reserve, so the action cannot check or deplete one.
tests: A positive quantity adds that much graphite to the miners' stock. A zero or negative quantity is refused.
semantic_bindings: quantity: graphite mined and added to the miners' stock

mechanics.rationale: Lead makers use graphite from the miners and clay held at the lead works to make leads. The locations are separate, so graphite is treated as an order from afar; clay is consumed at the lead works.

checks.label: the lead works has enough clay

limits: The separated parties' order is represented as immediate; no transport state links the miners and lead works.
tests: With sufficient graphite and clay, the action consumes both inputs and adds the same quantity of leads. Either insufficient input refuses the action.
semantic_bindings: source: miners supplying graphite
quantity: graphite and clay consumed and leads made

mechanics.rationale: The factory consumes slats, leads, paint, erasers, and ferrules to assemble pencils. The mill and lead works are remote, so their stocks are treated as supplies ordered from afar.

checks.label: the lead works has enough leads

limits: Remote component orders are modeled as immediate transfers; the world has no represented stock in transit.
tests: With all five inputs sufficient, the action consumes the inputs and adds the requested pencils. An insufficient input refuses the action.
semantic_bindings: slat_source: mill supplying slats
lead_source: lead makers supplying leads
quantity: each input consumed and pencils assembled

mechanics.rationale: Packing at the factory consumes pencils and boxes and adds packed pencils.
limits: One packed-pencil stock unit represents one pencil packed; box capacity or packing time is not separately represented.
tests: With enough pencils and boxes, the action consumes both and adds the requested packed pencils. Insufficient inputs refuse it.
semantic_bindings: quantity: pencils and boxes consumed and packed pencils produced

mechanics.rationale: The carrier carries packed pencils from the factory source to the shop destination. The carrier's represented location is the road, so no same-place check is imposed; stock transfer is represented directly because no in-transit goods or destination reference can be retained in the available state.

checks.label: the factory has enough packed pencils

limits: Delivery is modeled as an immediate stock transfer. The represented state cannot store a destination, goods in transit, or a delivery countdown on the carrier.
tests: With enough packed pencils at the factory, the action transfers the requested quantity to the shop. Insufficient stock refuses it.
semantic_bindings: source: factory stock being carried
to: shop receiving packed pencils
quantity: packed pencils transferred

mechanics.rationale: A sale is one pencil per action under the represented money rule. The listed shop price is charged once, and the shop transfers one packed pencil to the customer. The parties' different locations make this an afar purchase.

checks.label: the shop listed a positive price
the customer can pay the listed price
the shop has a packed pencil to sell

limits: The action's quantity is ignored: each sale transfers exactly one pencil and charges the listed price once. The afar purchase is immediate because no order or delivery state is represented.
tests: If the customer can pay and the shop has a packed pencil, one pencil transfers and the listed price moves from customer cash to shop cash. A customer unable to pay or a shop without stock is refused.
semantic_bindings: shop: seller and recipient of payment
customer: buyer and payer
quantity: one pencil per sale, regardless of requested quantity

processes.rationale: Ongoing production needs renewing raw-material stocks. The represented logger and miner stocks are the only available raw-material stocks; this renewal does not create slats, leads, or finished products.

checks.label: the logging crew or miners have not reached the stock ceiling

readout.title: How goods moved through the chain
readout.summary: The lead-maker made leads, the mill turned cedar logs into slats, and the factory assembled and packed pencils. The carrier moved packed pencils to the shop, where the shop sold them to the customer; the events do not show work stalled while waiting for supplies.

mechanisms.name: Demand reached and met
